attributes.name: mode
attributes.digest: Display mode
attributes.description: Sets theobject's mode of operation.: (the default) Only one note can be selected and displayed at one time.: Theobject keeps track of note-ons and note-offs, so it mirrors which notes are currently held down on your MIDI keyboard. A key is “turned off” by sending theobject a key on message with a velocity of 0.

attributes.name: param_connect
attributes.digest: Connect to Parameter
attributes.description: Establishes a two-way connection between the object and a parameter of a compatible object with parameters such asor. The object can be used to change the value of the parameter and will update if the parameter value changes. The easiest way to setis with the attribute's menu in theor the Connect submenu of the. The menu displays all available parameters of compatible objects.Setting theattribute with a message requires the target parameter's path, which is the host object's scriping name followed by two colons and the parameter name. For example, for aobject with scripting name, the path of theparameter would be. You can set a value for thebefore the host object or parameter exists, and the object will connect to the parameter once it exists. Refer to the user guide entry forfor more details.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: also sends out numbers when you click or drag on it with the mouse. The velocity value is determined by the previous value received in the right inlet.If theobject is in polyphonic mode, you need to click on a note twice: once to send a note-on and draws the note, and once again to send a note-off and erase the note.

messages.name: anything
messages.description: Notes can also be added using the musical note name and octave, i.e., F#3. This is especially useful for forcing display of accidentals (# or b). For example, a value of 59 and the message Cb4 both produce the same note, but the number will display a B note while the message displays a C-flat.

messages.name: bang
messages.description: In left inlet: Sends out the pitch and velocity values currently stored in.

messages.name: chord
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a list of MIDI note name and velocity pairs, can be used to play chords on thein polyphonic mode (set by themessage). Themessage sends note-offs for currently held notes, followed by note-on commands for the specified note and velocity pairs. When theobject's state is saved by aobject in polyphonic mode, theobject will storemessages.

messages.name: clear
messages.description: In left inlet: Themessage will clear any notes on the staves, but will not trigger any output.

messages.name: float
messages.digest: Display and output a note value

messages.name: flush
messages.digest: Send note-off messages for all held notes
messages.description: In left inlet: When theobject is in polyphonic mode (set by themessage), themessage will send note-offs to currently held notes and clear theobject's display.

messages.name: in1
messages.description: In right inlet: The number received in the right inlet sets the output key velocity without triggering output.

messages.name: int
messages.digest: Display and output a note value
messages.description: The number received in the inlet is displayed graphically byif it falls within its displayed range. The current velocity value (from 1 to 127) thatholds is sent out its right outlet, followed by the received number out the left outlet.

messages.name: list
messages.digest: Set pitch and velocity, cause output
messages.description: A list of two numbers sent to the left inlet of nslider can be used to set and output the note and velocity values.

messages.name: set
messages.digest: Set pitch and velocity with no output
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a number, changes the value displayed by, without triggering output. If themessage is followed by two numbers, both the note and velocity values are set, without causing output.
